Point-by-point on audit3 counterevidence:

(1) section_id dual surface — REJECT as force-to-anchor-3. Rubric D3=5 explicitly requires aliases document winner + deprecation; contract does both (correlation_id wins; removed in v4). Failure pattern #6 is dual names forever with no winner — not this case. Residual compat surface is mild bloat, not silent dual meaning (hard gate 3 still passes).

(2) output_profile + include dual Response shapers — PARTIAL ACCEPT. custom = include-only is stated; non-custom merge when both set is underspecified → partial precedence on one output attribute. That alone is a good-not-excellent ding (drops from 5 toward 4), not enough for full anchor-3 collapse when the rest of the surface is orthogonal.

(3) standard candidates[] + learning_log_row + top-level status as audit echo — REJECT misclassification. Pattern #5 names resolution + tags + field_build; those are full-only (call-contract 186-190). D2 itself requires an optional log row for thin hosts; learning_log_row restating decision/paths is the thin-host log product, not an audit-echo stack. Top-level status is the aggregate status enum, not a third narrative of the same candidate fields.

(4) human_feedback multi-role (content + situation claim + intent-inference source) — REJECT as non-overlap failure. One content field with documented multi-source derivation is the lean alternative to parallel channels (context_hints removed). Intent and situation precedence are stated; that is D3 strength, not dual-field soup.

Net: fields are largely one-job-per-field with stated multi-source precedence and a documented alias winner. Residual mild output dual-control and intentional log-row restatement prevent D3=5. They do not match anchor 3 better than anchor 4 (good). ≥4 threshold satisfied; verdict pass.
